# Roadmap

_`Status` is each milestone's **current** delivery status, derived from krill's append-only `milestone_status_event` history (`store.MilestoneStatusEventStore.CurrentStatuses`). A milestone with no recorded transition is `not started` — that is krill's own derivation from the absence of history, not a rendered default._

13 milestones (1 abandoned), one block each below.

### M1 — An Agent can pull exactly the spec slice its task touches out of krill, for a product whose brief now lives in krill and is rendered back into the repo

- Status: shipped
- Delivers: C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, C6, C7, C8, C9
- Must not foreclose: LB1, LB2, LB3, LB4, LB5, LB6, LB7
- Deliberately deferred: Design sessions: holding a design session in krill with each draft kept as a revision record (C10), and querying what is still open in one (C11). (→ M2); Mediated intake for the Requirement Contributor (C12): plain-language ideas shaped into conforming entities by a producer-role Agent. Deferred, not papered over. (→ M2); Adoption of a product krill did not author: importing it and rendering it back faithfully (C27). (→ M2); Authoring the delivery axis, i.e. cutting a product into milestones and milepebbles (C13), and delivery-status visibility (C28). M1 holds and renders milestones that arrive inside an imported document and authors none, because the delivery axis is an association, never a second parent of an entity. (→ M3); The entire work surface: claiming a task with a self-contained payload (C14), reporting a run's outcome (C15), resuming a task on any host (C16), and recording scope notes with their own lifecycle (C25). (→ M4); Operator console (C17), intervention and escalation on stuck tasks (C18), and unattended swarm operation (C26). (→ M5); Web UI for any persona (C19), with the UI's own work tracked in krill as the dogfood case. (→ Later); Krill owning the branch and PR lifecycle for a task (C20); M1 only holds references to them. (→ Later); Drift detection: telling an operator when a product's spec in krill has drifted from the code that implements it (C21). (→ Later); Running a second repo or tenant on the same krill instance (C22). The scope column is present from M1 because scope is a surrogate key on every row. (→ Later); Cross-product decisions: recording a decision that spans several products (C23). (→ Later); Agent identity: attributing an action to a specific agent rather than only to the run and the human who minted it (C24). The column shape is present from M1 because every mutation records two subjects. (→ Later)
- FR budget: 12

### M2 — A Requirement Contributor can bring an idea to krill in plain language and watch a producer-role Agent turn it into spec entities through a recorded design session, on a product krill did not write

- Status: shipped
- Delivers: C10, C11, C12, C27
- Must not foreclose: LB1, LB2, LB3, LB4, LB5, LB7

- FR budget: 12

### M3 — A Requirement Contributor can cut a krill product into shippable milestones and agent-shippable milepebbles and see, from krill alone, what is planned versus what is merely spec'd

- Status: shipped
- Delivers: C13, C28
- Must not foreclose: LB2, LB3, LB6, LB7
- Deliberately deferred: the work surface (C14, C15, C16, C25) (→ M4); operator console and escalation (C17, C18, C26) (→ M5); branch/PR lifecycle (C20) (→ Later)

### M4 — An Agent can claim a task from krill, get everything it needs in the claim payload, report a verdict without knowing where the task goes next, and hand a half-finished task to a fresh run on another host

- Status: shipped
- Delivers: C14, C15, C16, C25
- Must not foreclose: LB1, LB3, LB4, LB6, LB7
- Deliberately deferred: the human-attention queue, the rejection-history carry, and all operator-facing escalation handling (C26) — M4 does not ship an uncapped loop: its reclaim path refuses to re-serve a task past its attempt cap, so what M5 adds is where exhausted work goes and who can see and act on it, not the stop itself (→ M5); operator console (C17, C18) (→ M5); krill owning branch/PR lifecycle (C20) (→ Later)
- FR budget: 12

### M5 — A Swarm Operator can leave the swarm running unattended and afterwards answer, from krill alone, what is claimed, what is stuck, what escalated to a human and why — and act on any of it without hand-editing storage

- Status: shipped
- Delivers: C17, C18, C26
- Must not foreclose: LB1, LB3, LB4
- Deliberately deferred: a web UI for the console (C19) — an API-only first cut satisfies this milestone and no web UI is required to close it (→ Later); krill owning branch/PR lifecycle (C20) (→ Later); drift detection (C21) (→ Later); second repo or tenant (C22) (→ Later); cross-product decisions (C23) (→ Later); agent identity (C24) (→ Later)
- FR budget: 12

### M6 — A Swarm Operator or a Requirement Contributor can do everything krill's console and design-session surfaces offer today from a browser, without an MCP client

- Status: shipped
- Delivers: C19, C29, C30, C31
- Must not foreclose: LB1, LB2, LB3, LB4, LB5, LB7
- Deliberately deferred: An Agent-facing UI. Agents keep MCP; no capability line proposed for one, and none should be — this is also what bounds M6's Delivers:C19 scope to the Swarm Operator and Requirement Contributor personas only. (→ Not scheduled — no roadmap entry; Agents are served over MCP indefinitely per the product vision); Krill owning branch and PR lifecycle for a task, not merely holding references to it (C20). (→ Later); Spec/code drift detection (C21). (→ Later); Running products from a second repository or tenant on the same krill instance (C22). (→ Later); Recording a decision that spans several products (C23). (→ Later); Attributing an action to a specific agent identity rather than only to the run and the human who minted it (C24). (→ Later)
- FR budget: 20

### M7 — A Requirement Contributor can correct anything krill holds — amend a Feature, FeatureSet, Milestone, Persona or Non-Goal, resolve a deferred one, void a mistaken create — and a Swarm Operator can read a milestone's delivery status unambiguously, so no row krill holds is ever permanently wrong.

- Status: shipped
- Delivers: C32, C33, C34
- Must not foreclose: LB2, LB3, LB4, LB5, LB6, LB7
- Deliberately deferred: Cluster 3 (M1-M5 delivery-surface defects) cut from M7 per architect's q-m7-coherence ruling: it does not serve M7's outcome sentence. The three defect NFRs re-homed as M8 scope (delivery/plugin defect triage Feature) together with #3027 (stale #2930 blocker asserted across 8 plugin files), #2962 (init_session kind enum lacks `agent`), and the propose_entities `position` tool-schema drift. FR-budget-neutral: cluster 3 is entirely NFRs, which do not count against M7's 14. (→ Follow-on milestone M8 (3f0b8d77-37eb-421d-892a-28b2d640840a) — created as the home for this cluster; its design session opens when M8 is picked up.); reparent_feature (M7's correction-surface-gaps milepebble, PR #3104) refuses cross-Product moves — a Feature can be reparented to a different FeatureSet within the same Product, but not moved to a different Product. This is stricter than the original M7 spec, which did not carve out that restriction. Shipped as-is deliberately rather than block the PR on resolving the design question. (→ A future milestone — revisit whether cross-Product Feature reparenting should be supported once a real use case for it shows up; until then the restriction stands as the safer default.)
- FR budget: 14

### M8 — Every delivery-surface defect found in M1-M5 is closed or tracked to a named owner, so a persona krill dispatches through a plugin actually gets the working, discoverable tool surface that plugin's docs and schema promise.

- Status: shipped
- Delivers: C36, C37
- Must not foreclose: LB2, LB3, LB6
- Deliberately deferred: Comment-integrity checker: a mechanism that greps krill's test, migration and tool-schema comments for cited identifiers and verifies each resolves. Deferred because it is a new capability with an unsettled false-positive policy, not a delivery-surface defect. The verified instances were admitted narrowly under M8. (→ Not admitted to any milestone; cut at the next roadmap re-cut if the false-positive policy is settled. Owner: the requester. Not a Non-Goal: the decision is unsettled.); Two intake items closed as already satisfied, with no Requirement: (1) the stale blocker text in the krill plugin docs claiming the task-lifecycle tools were unreachable from worker and validator personas (that blocker was already fixed; re-verified; GitHub issue #3027); (2) propose_entities `position` tool-schema drift, pinned by TestProposeEntities_SchemaHasNoCallerSettablePosition. Verification is recorded in M8's design session. (→ No future milestone: closed in place. A regression is a new defect for whichever milestone is in design.); HTTP GET routes for the void_event and non_goal_promotion registers, cut from M8 at stakeholder round 1. The read itself is not deferred: both registers are readable through the MCP audit tools. Only the second (HTTP) projection is deferred. (→ A console view of the void/cancel register, cut with the next operator-console work (C17, the operator console).); Tool-surface gap: no verb retracts a shipped Requirement, because void_entity refuses delivered entities and the delivery axis makes that permanent by design (shipped history is never rewritten). The related gap for un-shipped scope (no exposed backlog bucket id) was closed by M8's Requirement that the backlog read returns the bucket id ("Planned scope can be retracted from a milestone before it ships") and is no longer deferred. (→ Closed; the shipped-retraction case is a settled property of the delivery axis, not deferred work.); Two items stakeholders named for a destination, not admitted to M8: (1) console coverage gap: no ops view answers "unclaimed and idle"; (2) a Requirement cannot be retracted, only reworded, because deliveryRefusal (krill/store/void.go) refuses a void when any entity_milestone row exists. The premise of (2) is contested between two validator notes and must be settled before it can be scoped. (→ (1) The next console cut on the operator console (C17) and its browser version (C29), alongside the void/cancel register view. (2) A new capability cut at the next roadmap re-cut; owner is the requester. Neither is a Non-Goal: both decisions are unsettled.); Superseded: an earlier entry in this list wrongly said a Requirement was kept on M8 as the standing statement of the HTTP register routes. That text was corrected in place by amending the entry. No work moved and this entry adds no deferred work. (→ None: the HTTP register routes stay deferred to the next operator-console cut (C17), as stated in that earlier entry.); Superseded: the destinations of earlier entries in this list were corrected in place by amending those entries. No work moved and this entry adds no deferred work. (→ None: each earlier entry carries its own corrected destination (operator-console cut C17/C29, a roadmap re-cut, or closed in place).)
- FR budget: 2

### M13 — Operator UI facelift: a signed-in persona lands in a sidebar workspace shell with a product switcher and can tell at a glance what is stuck and which milestone is in flight, a Swarm Operator can browse tasks as a table or board and requeue, release or cancel stuck work in place, and a Requirement Contributor can follow milestones, read the spec and answer design-session questions, all from the browser.

- Status: planned
- Must not foreclose: LB1, LB3, LB4, LB6
- Ships alongside: Eight amended FRs that shipped in an earlier milestone and cannot be re-delivered (add_delivers refuses an entity another milestone delivers; shipped scope is never re-cut) are rewritten by the facelift and are built here, carried for planning by thin handle FRs that restate their unique obligations: 85a8b33c-3225-4200-9daf-aa50c9a2bed6 (shell) via P1 handle 41a7a34c; 9fcf870c-2fb0-4c96-97e2-d92b087a1646 (tasks table rows and order), b853922e-9a18-49b1-a819-569356633e3f (cut-milestone aggregation), 616778a6-c95f-488e-8962-366c5abe55d8 (write actions not foreclosed; pre-facelift task URLs kept) and d5a50ef0-21f4-499f-b914-64f4da030bc3 (list/board read-only rule) via P2a handle f41a352d; 4398c532-e8ed-4ac4-9ade-9be984b5cb2e (delivery/roadmap browse) and d20b75a8-8aeb-48ea-b703-729bcf75aff2 (task views reachable from Milestones) via P3a handle 31cbd3eb; 1f4c9eec-48e8-44dd-9fd3-f61d96bd5eb7 (task views show when loaded) via NFR 7b497d92 and the P2a handle. get_delivery_breakdown for the shipped milestones keeps showing them as shipped with the new, not-yet-built text. Also ships alongside: a P0 follow-up (note on Feature e2e03741) that the store refuses a manual escalate of a Done-lane task with a distinct named error mapped to 409; it adds no FR and does not hold P0.
- FR budget: 64
